intro: In B2 you met 'It is said that…' and 'He is said to…'. Now you'll report news, rumours and research like a journalist: many more reporting verbs, three infinitive forms that show when something happened, and 'There is believed to be…'. These patterns let you report a claim without saying who made it or whether it's true.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line (B2 taught it as a first look): It is said that this house is haunted / Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali. This lesson goes further: the full range of reporting verbs (said, reported, believed, thought, expected, estimated, known, considered, alleged, claimed, understood), the three infinitive forms and their time meaning, the tenses of be in both patterns, and the there-pattern. Purpose: news, reports and academic writing use these patterns to report a claim without naming its source and without saying it's true (distance from the claim, objective tone). Indonesian bridge: Dikabarkan bahwa… (It is reported that…), Konon… (It is said that… / X is said to…), Diperkirakan… (is estimated / is expected to), Diyakini… (is believed), Dianggap (is considered), Diketahui (is known), Diduga… (is thought/believed to; in crime and court news is alleged to have…, and the phrase to remember is suspected of + -ing).

Pattern 1: It + be + third form of a reporting verb + that + a full sentence (It is thought that the fire started at 2 a.m.). It is a dummy subject; the that-sentence keeps its own subject, verb and tense. be shows when the claim was made: It is believed / It was reported / It has been estimated. It is natural for numbers and whole situations (It is estimated that 10 million people…). hope, agree and decide work only in pattern 1: It is hoped that…, It was agreed that…, It has been decided that… ('The rules are hoped to…' is wrong). In formal writing keep 'that'.

Pattern 2: subject + be + third form + to-infinitive. The infinitive shows the action's time compared with the moment of saying: to + base = now or in general (He is thought to live in Bali; with expected, the future: The bridge is expected to open in May); to be + -ing = in progress now (The bank is believed to be preparing a new app); to have + third form = earlier (The singer is reported to have cancelled her tour), matching a past simple or present perfect in the that-sentence. State verbs (be, own, know, have) use to + base, not to be + -ing. With a past reporting verb the same logic is relative to that past moment: She was thought to be hiding in Medan; He was said to have left the company. Some verbs allow both to live / to be living (the continuous sounds more temporary): only test clear cases. Indonesian trap: Indonesian keeps one verb and adds a time word (dikabarkan mengundurkan diri kemarin), so learners write 'is reported resign' or 'is reported to resign yesterday'; English shows the time in the infinitive: is reported to have resigned. sedang → to be + -ing; sudah/kemarin → to have + third form; akan (with expected) → to + base.

Pattern 3: There + is/are + third form + to be + noun (There is thought to be a leak; There are believed to be more than 700 languages in Indonesia); earlier: to have been (There is said to have been an argument). The verb agrees with the noun after it (is + a leak, are + two leaks). Indonesian trap: Diduga ada masalah: ada is sometimes translated as have (Saya ada mobil), so learners write 'There is believed to have a problem'; in this pattern the infinitive is always to be (or to have been). No that after there ('There is believed that…' → It is believed that there is…).

Common errors to correct: 'He is said that he left the company' (mixes the patterns) → He is said to have left the company / It is said that he left the company; 'There is believed to have a problem with the system' → to be; 'The minister is reported resign yesterday' → is reported to have resigned; 'to resigned', 'to has resigned' (after to, the base form); 'is believed to leave last week' (earlier → to have left); 'is known to' (accepted fact) vs 'is known as' (dikenal sebagai, a name); 'is alleged' for unproven accusations, not 'is known'. cancelled (British) / canceled (American); rumoured / rumored.

Scope: no inversion, cleft sentences or the subjunctive in examples. Passive infinitives (The bridge is thought to have been built in 1890) and the adverbs reportedly / allegedly may be explained briefly if asked, but aren't taught or tested. Both pattern 1 and pattern 2 are equally formal; choosing between them is style (topic first → pattern 2; numbers, long subjects or hope/agree/decide → pattern 1), so questions must say which pattern to use.

keyPoints.title: Pattern 1: It is thought that…
keyPoints.explanation: It + be + the third form of a reporting verb + that + a full sentence. It means nothing; the news is in the that-sentence, which keeps its own subject, verb and tense. be shows when the claim was made: It is believed…, It was reported…, It has been estimated…. hope, agree and decide work only in this pattern: It is hoped that…, It was agreed that….

examples.en: It is estimated that 10 million people use the app every day.
examples.id: Diperkirakan 10 juta orang memakai aplikasi itu setiap hari.

examples.en: It was reported that the flight had been delayed for six hours.
examples.id: Dikabarkan penerbangan itu tertunda enam jam.

examples.en: It has been decided that the office will close on Fridays.
examples.id: Sudah diputuskan bahwa kantor akan tutup setiap hari Jumat.

id.title: Pola 1: It is thought that…
id.explanation: It + be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + that + kalimat lengkap. It tidak punya arti; beritanya ada di kalimat setelah that, yang tetap punya subjek, kata kerja dan tense sendiri. be menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat: It is believed…, It was reported…, It has been estimated…. hope, agree dan decide hanya bisa dipakai di pola ini: It is hoped that…, It was agreed that….

keyPoints.title: Pattern 2: He is said to… with three infinitives
keyPoints.explanation: Subject + be + the third form of a reporting verb + to-infinitive. The infinitive shows when the action happens: to + base form = now or in general (with expected: later), to be + -ing = in progress now (sedang), to have + third form = earlier (sudah, kemarin). Never drop 'to' and never mix with 'that': 'He is said that he left' ✗, 'is reported resign' ✗.

examples.en: He is thought to live in Bali.
The bank is believed to be preparing a new app.
examples.id: Bank itu diyakini sedang menyiapkan aplikasi baru.

examples.en: The singer is reported to have cancelled her tour.
examples.id: Penyanyi itu dikabarkan sudah membatalkan turnya.

id.title: Pola 2: He is said to… dengan tiga bentuk infinitif
id.explanation: Subjek + be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + to-infinitive. Infinitifnya menunjukkan kapan tindakannya terjadi: to + bentuk dasar = sekarang atau secara umum (dengan expected: nanti), to be + -ing = sedang berlangsung, to have + bentuk ketiga = lebih dulu (sudah, kemarin). Jangan buang 'to' dan jangan campur dengan 'that': 'He is said that he left' ✗, 'is reported resign' ✗.

keyPoints.title: Pattern 3: There is believed to be…
keyPoints.explanation: When the news is that something exists (ada): There + is/are + the third form of a reporting verb + to be + noun. is/are agrees with the noun after it. For something earlier, use to have been. Indonesian 'ada' here means 'there is', so it's always 'to be', never 'to have' + noun.

examples.en: There is thought to be a leak in the gas pipe.
examples.id: Diduga ada kebocoran di pipa gas itu.

examples.en: There are believed to be more than 700 languages in Indonesia.
examples.id: Diyakini ada lebih dari 700 bahasa di Indonesia.

examples.en: There is said to have been an argument before the meeting.
examples.id: Konon sempat ada pertengkaran sebelum rapat.

id.title: Pola 3: There is believed to be…
id.explanation: Kalau beritanya adalah bahwa sesuatu ada: There + is/are + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + to be + kata benda. is/are mengikuti kata benda sesudahnya. Untuk sesuatu yang lebih dulu, pakai to have been. Kata 'ada' di sini artinya 'there is', jadi selalu 'to be', tidak pernah 'to have' + kata benda.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'It is reported that': The ferry is reported to be stuck near Lombok.
expected: it is reported that the ferry is stuck near lombok
it's reported that the ferry is stuck near lombok
guidedPractice.hint: to be = now, so the that-sentence uses 'is'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right infinitive of 'own' (a state verb, true now): The businessman is thought ___ three hotels in Bali.
guidedPractice.hint: A state that's true now → to + base form (not to be + -ing).

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'The new terminal' (pattern: is expected to + verb): It is expected that the new terminal will open in 2028.
expected: the new terminal is expected to open in 2028
guidedPractice.hint: With expected, to + base form already points to the future: no 'will'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: There is believed to have a gas leak in the building.
expected: there is believed to be a gas leak in the building
it is believed that there is a gas leak in the building
guidedPractice.hint: 'ada' here means 'there is', so the infinitive is to be.

independentPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The suspect is said that he escaped through the window.
expected: the suspect is said to have escaped through the window
it is said that the suspect escaped through the window
independentPractice.hint: Either start with It (It is said that…) or keep the suspect and use to have + third form for something earlier.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with the present passive of 'report' and the right form for something earlier: There ___ three small earthquakes in the area last week.
independentPractice.hint: earthquakes is plural → are; last week → to have been.

assessment.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'It is believed that': The data leak is believed to have come from a former employee.
acceptableAnswers: it is believed that the data leak came from a former employee
it's believed that the data leak came from a former employee
it is believed the data leak came from a former employee
it is believed that the data leak has come from a former employee
assessment.rubric: Correct: It is believed that the data leak came from a former employee (pattern 1: It + is believed + that + a full sentence; 'to have come' = earlier → past simple 'came'). 'has come' is accepted (grammatical, but 'came' is more natural). 'It is believed that the data leak comes from…' = 50 (loses the earlier time). 'It is believed that the data leak to have come…' = 20 (after that, a full sentence with its own verb). 'It is believed that the data leak come…' = 40 (needs the past form). 'It was believed…' = 60 (people believe it now → is). Leaving out 'data' = 90.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the passive of 'hope' (pattern 1): ___ that the new rules will reduce traffic in the city centre.
assessment.rubric: Correct: It is hoped (pattern 1: It + is + third form + that; hope works only in this pattern, and will shows the hope is now). 'The new rules are hoped' = 10 (hope can't be used in pattern 2). 'It hopes' = 20 (active: says 'it' does the hoping). 'It is hope' = 40 (needs the third form hoped). 'It was hoped' = 60 (a past hope would go with would, not will). 'It is hoping' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right infinitive of 'approve': The head of the hospital is said ___ the purchase last year without a tender.
assessment.rubric: Correct: to have approved (pattern 2; last year = earlier than the moment of saying → to have + third form). 'to approve' = 20 (now or in general, but the approval was last year). 'to approved' or 'to has approved' = 30 (after to, the base form: to have approved). 'have approved' = 50 (to is missing). 'to be approving' = 10 (in progress now). 'approved' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right infinitive of 'negotiate'. The talks are still going on: the two airlines are understood ___ a merger.
assessment.rubric: Correct: to be negotiating (pattern 2; the talks are in progress now → to be + -ing). 'to negotiate' = 50 (grammatical, but sounds like a general fact or a plan, not talks happening now). 'to have negotiated' = 30 (says the talks are already finished). 'to be negotiate' = 40 (needs the -ing form). 'negotiating' or 'be negotiating' = 40 (to is missing).

assessment.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'The former head of the agency': It is alleged that the former head of the agency used public money to buy a luxury car.
acceptableAnswers: the former head of the agency is alleged to have used public money to buy a luxury car
the former head of the agency is alleged to have used public money for a luxury car
assessment.rubric: Correct: The former head of the agency is alleged to have used public money to buy a luxury car (pattern 2; 'used' = earlier → to have + third form). 'is alleged to use' = 30 (now or in general, but the action was earlier). 'is alleged that he used…' = 20 (mixes the patterns: that needs It at the start). 'is alleged to have use' = 50 (needs the third form used). 'is alleged to used' = 30. 'was alleged to have used' = 70 (the claim is made now → is). Small changes to the rest of the sentence that keep the meaning = 90.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the passive of 'say' and the right infinitive: There ___ a serious shortage of nurses at the hospital at the moment.
assessment.rubric: Correct: is said to be (pattern 3: There + is + said + to be; 'ada' = there is, and 'at the moment' → now). 'is said to have' = 20 (to have + noun is the classic mistake: it must be to be). 'is said to have been' = 40 (says the shortage was earlier, but it's happening at the moment). 'are said to be' = 50 (a shortage is singular → is). 'is said that there is' = 30 (that needs It: It is said that there is…). 'is said being' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the passive of 'estimate' and the right infinitive: There ___ more than 2,000 unlicensed clinics in the province.
assessment.rubric: Correct: are estimated to be (pattern 3: There + are + estimated + to be; clinics is plural → are). 'is estimated to be' = 50 (the verb agrees with 'clinics' → are). 'are estimated to have' = 20 (ada = there are → to be, not to have). 'are estimated to have been' = 60 (says the clinics existed earlier; nothing in the sentence says so). 'are estimating to be' = 10 (active). 'are estimated that there are' = 20.

material.title: Who says so? Keeping a distance from the claim

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B2: you met two news-style patterns, *It **is said that** this house is haunted* and *Pak Hasan **is said to have moved** to Bali*. In this lesson you'll use them like a journalist or a researcher: with many more verbs, with every time (now, in progress, earlier, later), and with a third pattern that starts with **there**.

**Why do writers use them?** They report what people say, think or believe **without naming who** said it and **without saying it's true**. The writer keeps a **distance from the claim** (menjaga jarak: 'begitu kata orang, kami belum memastikan'). That's why these patterns are everywhere in news, reports and academic writing: the tone stays **formal and objective** (netral, tidak memihak).

**The Indonesian bridge:** you already do this in Indonesian. *Dikabarkan bahwa…*, *Diduga…*, *Konon…*, *Diperkirakan…*, *Diyakini…* do exactly the same job. The difference: Indonesian puts one *di-* word in front and leaves the rest of the sentence alone, while English needs a fixed shape: **It is … that…**, or **subject + is … + to…**.

Each **reporting verb** (a verb for saying or thinking) has its own job. Look at the notes below.

id.text:
Ringkasan singkat dari B2: kamu sudah kenal dua pola gaya berita, *It **is said that** this house is haunted* dan *Pak Hasan **is said to have moved** to Bali*. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan memakainya seperti wartawan atau peneliti: dengan lebih banyak kata kerja, dengan semua waktu (sekarang, sedang berlangsung, lebih dulu, nanti), dan dengan pola ketiga yang diawali **there**.

**Kenapa penulis memakainya?** Pola ini melaporkan apa yang dikatakan, dipikirkan atau diyakini orang **tanpa menyebut siapa** yang mengatakannya dan **tanpa menyatakan bahwa itu benar**. Penulisnya menjaga **jarak dari klaim** itu ('begitu kata orang, kami belum memastikan'). Karena itu pola ini ada di mana-mana dalam berita, laporan dan tulisan akademik: nadanya tetap **formal dan objektif** (netral, tidak memihak).

**Jembatan dari bahasa Indonesia:** kamu sebenarnya sudah melakukannya. *Dikabarkan bahwa…*, *Diduga…*, *Konon…*, *Diperkirakan…*, *Diyakini…* punya tugas yang persis sama. Bedanya: bahasa Indonesia cukup menaruh satu kata ber-*di-* di depan dan membiarkan sisa kalimatnya, sedangkan bahasa Inggris butuh bentuk yang tetap: **It is … that…**, atau **subjek + is … + to…**.

Setiap **kata kerja pelaporan** (kata kerja untuk mengatakan atau berpikir) punya tugasnya sendiri. Lihat catatan di bawah.

rows.en: The airline is reported to be in financial trouble.
rows.id: Maskapai itu dikabarkan sedang mengalami kesulitan keuangan.
rows.note: reported → dikabarkan, dilaporkan: news reports

id.note: reported → dikabarkan, dilaporkan: laporan berita

rows.en: The new vaccine is believed to be safe for children.
rows.id: Vaksin baru itu diyakini aman untuk anak-anak.
rows.note: believed / thought → diyakini, diduga: an opinion many people hold

id.note: believed / thought → diyakini, diduga: pendapat yang dipegang banyak orang

rows.en: Rice prices are expected to fall after the harvest.
rows.id: Harga beras diperkirakan turun setelah panen.
rows.note: expected → diperkirakan akan: the future

id.note: expected → diperkirakan akan: masa depan

rows.en: The project is estimated to cost Rp4 trillion.
rows.id: Proyek itu diperkirakan menelan biaya Rp4 triliun.
rows.note: estimated → diperkirakan: numbers, costs, amounts

id.note: estimated → diperkirakan: angka, biaya, jumlah

rows.en: Smoking is known to cause lung cancer.
rows.id: Merokok diketahui menyebabkan kanker paru-paru.
rows.note: known to → diketahui: an accepted fact (different from 'is known as' = dikenal sebagai)

id.note: known to → diketahui: fakta yang sudah diakui (beda dengan 'is known as' = dikenal sebagai)

rows.en: Bu Ani is considered to be the best negotiator in the team.
rows.id: Bu Ani dianggap negosiator terbaik di timnya.
rows.note: considered → dianggap; 'to be' is often left out: is considered the best

id.note: considered → dianggap; 'to be' sering dihilangkan: is considered the best

rows.en: The former manager is alleged to have stolen Rp2 billion.
rows.id: Mantan manajer itu diduga mencuri Rp2 miliar.
rows.note: alleged → diduga: an accusation that isn't proven yet (crime and court news)

id.note: alleged → diduga: tuduhan yang belum terbukti (berita kriminal dan pengadilan)

rows.en: The supplement is claimed to cure diabetes.
rows.id: Suplemen itu diklaim bisa menyembuhkan diabetes.
rows.note: claimed → diklaim: someone says so, and the writer doubts it

id.note: claimed → diklaim: ada yang bilang begitu, dan penulisnya meragukannya

rows.en: The two banks are understood to be in talks.
rows.id: Kabarnya kedua bank itu sedang berunding.
rows.note: understood → kabarnya: from a source the newspaper doesn't name

id.note: understood → kabarnya: dari sumber yang tidak disebut oleh koran itu

blocks.text: **Diduga** has several English partners. For an opinion: *is thought / is believed to*. For an accusation that isn't proven: *is alleged to*, which journalists choose carefully because it says 'this is a claim, not a fact'. And a phrase to remember: *is suspected **of** + -ing* (after *of*, use -ing): *He is suspected of leaking the data.* Don't use *is known to* for an accusation: *known* says it's an accepted fact.

id.text: **Diduga** punya beberapa pasangan dalam bahasa Inggris. Untuk pendapat: *is thought / is believed to*. Untuk tuduhan yang belum terbukti: *is alleged to*, yang dipilih wartawan dengan hati-hati karena artinya 'ini klaim, bukan fakta'. Dan satu frasa untuk diingat: *is suspected **of** + -ing* (setelah *of*, pakai -ing): *He is suspected of leaking the data.* Jangan pakai *is known to* untuk tuduhan: *known* berarti itu fakta yang sudah diakui.

blocks.prompt: A footballer is accused of match-fixing, but nothing has been proven in court yet. Which sentence keeps the right distance?
options: The player is known to have fixed three matches.
The player is alleged to have fixed three matches.
The player is considered fixing three matches.
blocks.explain: alleged = accused, not proven (diduga), which is exactly the situation. known says it's an accepted fact, which the reporter can't say yet. 'is considered fixing' is not grammatical: considered needs to + verb.

id.prompt: Seorang pemain sepak bola dituduh mengatur skor, tapi belum ada yang terbukti di pengadilan. Kalimat mana yang menjaga jarak dengan tepat?
id.explain: alleged = dituduh, belum terbukti (diduga), persis situasinya. known berarti fakta yang sudah diakui, padahal wartawannya belum bisa mengatakan itu. 'is considered fixing' tidak gramatikal: considered perlu to + kata kerja.

id.title: Siapa yang bilang? Menjaga jarak dari klaim

blocks.text:
**It + be + the third form of a reporting verb + that + a full sentence.**

*People think that the flood damaged 500 houses* → ***It is thought that** the flood damaged 500 houses.*

The *It* means nothing: it's a 'dummy' subject (subjek pengisi, seperti *It* di *It's raining*). The real news is in the *that* part, which stays a normal, complete sentence with its own subject, verb and tense: *It is thought that the fire **started** at 2 a.m.*

**be shows when the claim was made**, so it can be in any tense: *It **is** believed that…* (people believe it now), *It **was** reported that…* (the report came in the past), *It **has been** estimated that…* (a recent estimate).

**When is pattern 1 the natural choice?** When the news is a number or a whole situation (*It is estimated that 10 million people…*), or when the subject would be very long. And three verbs work **only** in this pattern: **hope, agree, decide** (*It is hoped that…* = diharapkan, *It was agreed that…* = disepakati, *It has been decided that…* = sudah diputuskan). 'The new rules are hoped to…' ✗.

In speech *that* is often dropped (*It's said he's moving to Singapore*), but in formal writing keep it.

id.text:
**It + be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + that + kalimat lengkap.**

*People think that the flood damaged 500 houses* → ***It is thought that** the flood damaged 500 houses.*

*It* di sini tidak punya arti: ia subjek 'pengisi' (seperti *It* di *It's raining*). Beritanya yang sebenarnya ada di bagian *that*, yang tetap kalimat biasa dan lengkap dengan subjek, kata kerja dan tense-nya sendiri: *It is thought that the fire **started** at 2 a.m.*

**be menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat**, jadi bisa dalam tense apa saja: *It **is** believed that…* (orang meyakininya sekarang), *It **was** reported that…* (laporannya muncul di masa lalu), *It **has been** estimated that…* (perkiraan yang baru saja dibuat).

**Kapan pola 1 jadi pilihan yang wajar?** Kalau beritanya berupa angka atau satu situasi utuh (*It is estimated that 10 million people…*), atau kalau subjeknya akan sangat panjang. Dan ada tiga kata kerja yang **hanya** bisa dipakai di pola ini: **hope, agree, decide** (*It is hoped that…* = diharapkan, *It was agreed that…* = disepakati, *It has been decided that…* = sudah diputuskan). 'The new rules are hoped to…' ✗.

Dalam percakapan *that* sering dihilangkan (*It's said he's moving to Singapore*), tapi dalam tulisan formal pertahankan.

rows.id: Diperkirakan 10 juta orang memakai aplikasi itu setiap hari.
rows.note: a number → pattern 1 is natural

id.note: angka → pola 1 terasa wajar

rows.en: It was reported that the flight had been delayed for six hours.
rows.id: Dikabarkan penerbangan itu tertunda enam jam.
rows.note: was reported: the report came in the past; the delay happened before it (had been delayed)

id.note: was reported: laporannya muncul di masa lalu; keterlambatannya terjadi sebelum itu (had been delayed)

rows.en: It is thought that the fire started in the warehouse.
rows.id: Kebakaran itu diduga bermula di gudang.
rows.note: the that-sentence keeps its own tense (started)

rows.en: It has been decided that the office will close on Fridays.
rows.id: Sudah diputuskan bahwa kantor akan tutup setiap hari Jumat.

blocks.text: Don't mix the patterns. With **that**, start with **It**: *It is said that he left the company.* With the person at the start, use **to**: *He is said to have left the company.* 'He is said **that** he left' ✗ gives one verb two subjects (*he* … *he*).

id.text: Jangan campur polanya. Kalau pakai **that**, mulai dengan **It**: *It is said that he left the company.* Kalau orangnya di awal, pakai **to**: *He is said to have left the company.* 'He is said **that** he left' ✗ membuat satu kata kerja punya dua subjek (*he* … *he*).

blocks.prompt: ___ that the merger will create 2,000 new jobs.
blocks.explain: Pattern 1: It + is + expected + that + a full sentence. 'It expects' is active: it says 'it' is doing the expecting. 'There is expected' doesn't work with that: the there-pattern needs to be + a noun.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ that the merger will create 2,000 new jobs.
id.explain: Pola 1: It + is + expected + that + kalimat lengkap. 'It expects' itu aktif: artinya 'it' yang memperkirakan. 'There is expected' tidak bisa dipakai dengan that: pola there perlu to be + kata benda.

material.title: Pattern 2: He is said to… and the three infinitives

blocks.text:
**Subject + be + the third form of a reporting verb + to-infinitive.** The person or thing in the news comes first, which keeps your text focused on its topic: *The minister is reported to…*, *The bridge is expected to…*.

The **infinitive** (to + verb) changes to show **when** the action happens, compared with the moment people say or believe it:
- **to + base form** = now or in general: *He is thought **to live** in Bali* (he lives there now). With *expected*, it points to the **future**: *The bridge is expected **to open** in May.*
- **to be + -ing** = in progress right now, like *sedang*: *The bank is believed **to be preparing** a new app.*
- **to have + third form** = **earlier**, like *sudah* or *kemarin*: *The singer is reported **to have cancelled** her tour* (cancelled: British; canceled: American).

**The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian keeps the same verb and lets a time word do the work: *Menteri itu dikabarkan mengundurkan diri **kemarin***. English must show the time **inside the infinitive**: 'is reported **resign** yesterday' ✗ (no *to*), 'is reported **to resign** yesterday' ✗ (wrong time) → *is reported **to have resigned** yesterday*. After *to*, the verb is always in its base form: 'to resigned' ✗, 'to has resigned' ✗.

**be still shows when the claim was made.** With a past reporting verb, measure from that past moment: *She **was thought to be hiding** in Medan* (at that time), *He **was said to have left** the company* (before that time).

id.text:
**Subjek + be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + to-infinitive.** Orang atau benda yang diberitakan ada di depan, jadi tulisanmu tetap fokus pada topiknya: *The minister is reported to…*, *The bridge is expected to…*.

**Infinitif** (to + kata kerja) berubah untuk menunjukkan **kapan** tindakannya terjadi, dibandingkan dengan saat orang mengatakan atau meyakininya:
- **to + bentuk dasar** = sekarang atau secara umum: *He is thought **to live** in Bali* (dia tinggal di sana sekarang). Dengan *expected*, artinya **masa depan**: *The bridge is expected **to open** in May.*
- **to be + -ing** = sedang berlangsung sekarang, seperti *sedang*: *The bank is believed **to be preparing** a new app.*
- **to have + bentuk ketiga** = **lebih dulu**, seperti *sudah* atau *kemarin*: *The singer is reported **to have cancelled** her tour* (cancelled: British; canceled: Amerika).

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia memakai kata kerja yang sama dan membiarkan kata waktu yang bekerja: *Menteri itu dikabarkan mengundurkan diri **kemarin***. Bahasa Inggris harus menunjukkan waktunya **di dalam infinitif**: 'is reported **resign** yesterday' ✗ (tanpa *to*), 'is reported **to resign** yesterday' ✗ (waktunya salah) → *is reported **to have resigned** yesterday*. Setelah *to*, kata kerjanya selalu bentuk dasar: 'to resigned' ✗, 'to has resigned' ✗.

**be tetap menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat.** Kalau kata kerja pelaporannya past, hitung dari saat di masa lalu itu: *She **was thought to be hiding** in Medan* (pada waktu itu), *He **was said to have left** the company* (sebelum waktu itu).

blocks.text: *to be* has two jobs. In *He is said **to be** very rich*, *be* is just the base form of *is* (to + base form: now). In *He is said **to be working** abroad*, it's to be + -ing (in progress). With a **state verb** (a verb for a state, not an action: *be, own, know, have, cost*), use to + base form: *She is thought **to own** three hotels*, not 'to be owning'. With *live* or *work* both are fine (*to live / to be living in Bali*); the -ing form sounds more temporary.

id.text: *to be* punya dua tugas. Di *He is said **to be** very rich*, *be* hanyalah bentuk dasar dari *is* (to + bentuk dasar: sekarang). Di *He is said **to be working** abroad*, itu to be + -ing (sedang berlangsung). Dengan **kata kerja keadaan** (kata kerja untuk keadaan, bukan tindakan: *be, own, know, have, cost*), pakai to + bentuk dasar: *She is thought **to own** three hotels*, bukan 'to be owning'. Dengan *live* atau *work* keduanya benar (*to live / to be living in Bali*); bentuk -ing terdengar lebih sementara.

blocks.prompt: It is thought that the hackers stole the data in March. → The hackers ___ the data in March.
blocks.explain: The stealing happened earlier (in March, past simple stole) → to have + third form: are thought to have stolen. 'to steal' is for now or in general, and 'to stolen' breaks the rule that after to comes the base form.

id.prompt: Ubah polanya: It is thought that the hackers stole the data in March. → The hackers ___ the data in March.
id.explain: Pencuriannya terjadi lebih dulu (bulan Maret, past simple stole) → to have + bentuk ketiga: are thought to have stolen. 'to steal' untuk sekarang atau secara umum, dan 'to stolen' melanggar aturan bahwa setelah to harus bentuk dasar.

material.title: Pattern 3: There is believed to be…

blocks.text:
When the news is that something **exists** (*ada*), the subject is **there**, just like in *There is a problem*:

*People think there is a leak in the gas pipe* → ***There is thought to be** a leak in the gas pipe.*

**The shape: There + is/are + the third form of a reporting verb + to be + noun.** As with *there is / there are*, the verb agrees with the noun after it: *There **is** thought to be **a leak*** / *There **are** thought to be **two leaks***.

For something that existed **earlier**, use **to have been**: *There **is said to have been** an argument before the meeting.* And *be* shows when the claim was made: *There **was** thought to be no risk at the time.*

**The Indonesian trap:** *Diduga **ada** masalah di sistemnya.* Because *ada* is sometimes translated as *have* (*Saya ada mobil*), learners write 'There is believed **to have** a problem with the system' ✗. Here *ada* means *there is*, so the infinitive is always **to be** (or *to have been* for earlier), never 'to have' + noun: *There is believed **to be** a problem with the system.*

id.text:
Kalau beritanya adalah bahwa sesuatu **ada**, subjeknya **there**, sama seperti di *There is a problem*:

*People think there is a leak in the gas pipe* → ***There is thought to be** a leak in the gas pipe.*

**Bentuknya: There + is/are + bentuk ketiga kata kerja pelaporan + to be + kata benda.** Sama seperti *there is / there are*, kata kerjanya mengikuti kata benda sesudahnya: *There **is** thought to be **a leak*** / *There **are** thought to be **two leaks***.

Untuk sesuatu yang ada **lebih dulu**, pakai **to have been**: *There **is said to have been** an argument before the meeting.* Dan *be* menunjukkan kapan klaimnya dibuat: *There **was** thought to be no risk at the time.*

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Diduga **ada** masalah di sistemnya.* Karena *ada* kadang diterjemahkan jadi *have* (*Saya ada mobil*), banyak yang menulis 'There is believed **to have** a problem with the system' ✗. Di sini *ada* artinya *there is*, jadi infinitifnya selalu **to be** (atau *to have been* untuk yang lebih dulu), tidak pernah 'to have' + kata benda: *There is believed **to be** a problem with the system.*

blocks.text: Pattern 3 is pattern 2 with *there* as the subject, so the same rules apply: no *that* after it ('There is believed **that**…' ✗ → *It is believed that there is…*), and after *to* only **be** or **have been**.

id.text: Pola 3 adalah pola 2 dengan *there* sebagai subjeknya, jadi aturannya sama: tidak ada *that* sesudahnya ('There is believed **that**…' ✗ → *It is believed that there is…*), dan setelah *to* hanya **be** atau **have been**.

blocks.prompt: ___ hundreds of illegal gold mines in the area.
blocks.explain: ada = there are, so the infinitive is to be, and hundreds of mines is plural → are. 'to have' is the ada-trap, and 'There is' doesn't agree with the plural noun.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ hundreds of illegal gold mines in the area.
id.explain: ada = there are, jadi infinitifnya to be, dan hundreds of mines itu jamak → are. 'to have' adalah jebakan kata ada, dan 'There is' tidak cocok dengan kata benda jamak.

id.intro: Di B2 kamu sudah kenal 'It is said that…' dan 'He is said to…'. Sekarang kamu akan melaporkan berita, kabar dan hasil penelitian seperti wartawan: lebih banyak kata kerja pelaporan, tiga bentuk infinitif yang menunjukkan kapan sesuatu terjadi, dan 'There is believed to be…'. Pola-pola ini memungkinkan kamu melaporkan sebuah klaim tanpa menyebut siapa yang membuatnya atau apakah itu benar.
suggestedQuestions: Kapan aku pakai 'to have done' dan kapan 'to be doing' setelah 'is said'?
Kenapa aku bisa bilang 'It is hoped that…' tapi tidak bisa 'The plan is hoped to…'?
Kenapa 'There is believed to be a problem', bukan 'to have a problem'?

assessment.cimp-1: Tulis ulang dalam bahasa Inggris, diawali dengan 'It is believed that': The data leak is believed to have come from a former employee.
assessment.cimp-2: Lengkapi dengan bentuk pasif dari 'hope' (pola 1): ___ that the new rules will reduce traffic in the city centre.
assessment.cimp-3: Lengkapi dengan bentuk infinitif yang tepat dari 'approve': The head of the hospital is said ___ the purchase last year without a tender.
assessment.cimp-4: Lengkapi dengan bentuk infinitif yang tepat dari 'negotiate'. Perundingannya masih berlangsung: the two airlines are understood ___ a merger.
assessment.cimp-5: Tulis ulang dalam bahasa Inggris, diawali dengan 'The former head of the agency': It is alleged that the former head of the agency used public money to buy a luxury car.
assessment.cimp-6: Lengkapi dengan bentuk pasif dari 'say' dan infinitif yang tepat: There ___ a serious shortage of nurses at the hospital at the moment.
assessment.cimp-7: Lengkapi dengan bentuk pasif dari 'estimate' dan infinitif yang tepat: There ___ more than 2,000 unlicensed clinics in the province.
